utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, all. [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case Number IT-95-9-A, The Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Simic, can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand? Thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Prosecution, I am Matthias Marcussen appearing with Ms. Barbara Goy and our case manager is Ms. Susan Grogan. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Appearances for the Defence for Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Mr. Pantelic and my co-counsel who is going to introduce himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Peter Murphy representing Blagoje Simic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as objective of this Status Conference is concerned, according to the Article 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, a Status Conference has to be held 120 days after the appeal has been raised. And this gives everybody the possibility to raise their objections and remarks. In this particular case, Mr. Simic filed his appeal on the 17th of November 2003, and the first Status Conference was held on the 5th of March 2004. This new Status Conference has for its goal to allow Mr. Simic to raise issues relative to the conditions of his detention and the condition of his mental and physical health. Mr. Simic or his Defence counsel, could you please advise the Trial Chamber in that particular order. Mr. Simic, you have the floor. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't have any health objections or any objections to my conditions of detention in the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may be seated. Does the Defence counsel for Mr. Simic have anything to add to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We are satisfied with the condition of our client, and I would like to underline that as his Defence team we have a very good cooperation with the OTP. They have provided us with certain documents relative to Article 68. It is our intention to file our submission today. We have finished our work concerning the appeals procedure. And we are here to help the Registry and our learned friends from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, counsel. We are very pleased to hear about the cooperation that has been taking place between the parties in the best interests of the proceedings that we're dealing with. And now, as concerns the appeal, we are here to inform the accused of the way the appeal is going. In the B/C/S version of the judgement, we have notified the accused of the date, 19 May 2004, when we're going -- that we are going to -- because of that, we have set the deadline tomorrow for the appeals to be filed. But now we have heard that this has already been done. I would also like to say that the request which has been filed by Franko Simatovic who requested access to the documents from the Bosanski Samac case is still before this Chamber. At this moment, I can't tell you anything else about that, but I would like to hear from the parties whether they have any objections or remarks, or do they have any issues to raise? Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm afraid I have to inform you that we have -- the Prosecution has not received a copy of the request for access to the file. So I'm afraid I'm not in a position to answer your question. As soon as we get back, we will look and see if we have received the documents. But, no, and I don't think we have received it. So we will check up on that with the Registry, and we can return to the Court quickly with an answer, I'm sure. I'm sorry about that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I hope you're going to be able to check the matter and inform us of your conclusions. I'm now turning towards the Defence, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. As far as the position of the Defence is concerned, we can inform you that we do not have any objections to this particular request. That is our position. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If there are no other issues to raise, the Status Conference may be adjourned at this point. It has been so decided.
